# ADR-0009: Tables measured from each engine; one oracle protocol

**Context.** Each engine pins its own Unicode version and definitions (Python `\w` is
`isalnum()`, V8 `\s` includes U+FEFF, Java folds with `toLowerCase(toUpperCase(c))`). Deriving
these from the Unicode spec would encode our assumptions, not the engines' behaviour.

**Decision.** Tables are generated by programs that run *inside the engine*: `tools/gen_python_tables.py`
(CPython 3.15.2), `tools/gen_js_tables.mjs` (V8 14.6), `tools/gen_go_tables.go` (Go 1.27.4, copying
`regexp/syntax`'s name resolution), `tools/GenJavaTables.java` (JDK 25.0.5.1). Where possible a
set is measured by running the engine's own regex on every scalar value. Parsers are ports of the
engines' parser sources read from the pinned images / OpenJDK tag. Real engines are reached through
`refract-oracle`: one JSON-lines protocol, a tiny runner per engine (native or pinned Docker image),
ASCII-escaped requests (Node's line reader splits on U+2028).

**Consequences.** Upgrading an engine means regenerating its table and re-running its oracle
suite. Engine versions are part of every report.
